turn1.explanation: The unit fires on clause- and sentence-boundary punctuation (commas, periods, semicolons) in running prose, most strongly when the document is about ships, boats or maritime topics. Weaker activations occur on the same punctuation in non-maritime, list-heavy or formal text such as news-production lists, legal citations and medical captions.
turn1.evidence: Nearly every marked token is a ',' '.' or ';', and the top examples are almost all ship/boat documents (SeaArk boats, powerships, a cruise-ship casino, Swedish listed ships, flying boats, V.Ships); words like 'ship' and 'boat' themselves are barely active. The weaker examples (anchor-electronics privacy policy, Google 'anchor text', TV news, a radiology caption) show the same punctuation firing at about 1.4–3.4 with little or no nautical content.
turn1.missing_data: Activations on the same punctuation in matched non-maritime documents, and a check of whether a maritime topic word alone (or words like 'anchor') raises punctuation activation later in a document, would show whether the topic modulation is real or a sampling artifact.
